78541-the-three-wise-men.title: The Three Wise Men
78541-the-three-wise-men.creator: Unknown
78541-the-three-wise-men.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. “Well, well,” rumbled the judge; “ain’t you got anybody in jail? Bring a couple of ’em up here and have ’em clean it out. You’re too easy on them jungle bums.” He shifted his big bulk about in the chair. “Every time I send a man to jail you fatten him up on your rest cure.

arxiv-1706-00437.title: DESY–17–067
arxiv-1706-00437.creator: IFT–UAM/CSIC–17–042
arxiv-1706-00437.description: A 2017 arXiv research paper by IFT–UAM/CSIC–17–042. The Next-to-Minimal Supersymmetric Standard model (NMSSM) appears as an interesting candidate for the interpretation of the Higgs-measurement at the LHC and as a rich framework embedding physics beyond the Standard Model. We consider the renormalization of the Higgs sector of this model in its 𝒞𝒫 {\cal CP} -violating version, and propose a renormalization scheme for the calculation of on-shell Higgs masses.

arxiv-1811-01248.title: Compressed Multiple Pattern Matching
arxiv-1811-01248.creator: Dmitry Kosolobov, Nikita Sivukhin
arxiv-1811-01248.description: Abstract Given d d strings over the alphabet { 0 , 1 , … , σ − 1 } \{0,1,\ldots,\sigma{-}1\} , the classical Aho–Corasick data structure allows us to find all o ​ c ​ c occ occurrences of the strings in any text T T in O ⁡ ( | T | + o ​ c ​ c )

arxiv-2103-10144.title: Model Independent Prediction of the Spectral Index of Primordial Quantum Fluctuations
arxiv-2103-10144.creator: Raul Jimenez
arxiv-2103-10144.description: Abstract One of the most important achievements of inflationary cosmology is to predict a departure from scale invariance of the power spectrum for cosmological scalar perturbations. This tilt is understood as a consequence of a quasi de Sitter classical equation of state describing the inflationary dark energy dominated era.

arxiv-2111-10084.title: On the application of Sylvester’s law of inertia to QUBO formulations for systems of linear equations
arxiv-2111-10084.creator: Sun Woo Park, Kyungtaek Jun
arxiv-2111-10084.description: Abstract Previous research on quantum annealing methods focused on effectively modeling systems of linear equations by utilizing quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) formulations. These studies take part in enhancing quantum computing algorithms, which extract properties of quantum computers suitable for improving classical computational models.

arxiv-2111-11212.title: Finding Useful Predictions by Meta-gradient Descent to Improve Decision-making
arxiv-2111-11212.creator: Alex Kearney, Anna Koop, Johannes Günther, Patrick M. Pilarski
arxiv-2111-11212.description: Abstract In computational reinforcement learning, a growing body of work seeks to express an agent’s model of the world through predictions about future sensations. In this manuscript we focus on predictions expressed as General Value Functions: temporally extended estimates of the accumulation of a future signal.

arxiv-2208-07809.title: Lifts of supersingular abelian varieties with small Mumford–Tate groups
arxiv-2208-07809.creator: Yeuk Hay Joshua Lam, Abhishek Oswal
arxiv-2208-07809.description: Abstract . We investigate to what extent an abelian variety over a finite field can be lifted to one in characteristic zero with small Mumford-Tate group. We prove that supersingular abelian surfaces, respectively threefolds, can be lifted to ones isogenous to a square, respectively product, of elliptic curves.

arxiv-2307-14267.title: Improving International Climate Policy via Mutually Conditional Binding Commitments (Track 2)
arxiv-2307-14267.creator: Jobst Heitzig, Jörg Oechssler, Christoph Pröschel, Niranjana Ragavan, Yat Long Lo
arxiv-2307-14267.description: Abstract The Paris Agreement, considered a significant milestone in climate negotiations, has faced challenges in effectively addressing climate change due to the unconditional nature of most Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs). This has resulted in a prevalence of free-riding behavior among major polluters and a lack of concrete conditionality in NDCs.

arxiv-2307-15039.title: EyeO: Autocalibrating Gaze Output with Gaze Input
arxiv-2307-15039.creator: Akanksha Saran, Jacob Alber, Cyril Zhang, Ann Paradiso, Danielle Bragg, John Langford, Microsoft Research NYC, Microsoft Research New England, Microsoft Research Redmond {akanksha.saran, jacob.alber, cyrilzhangannpar, danielle.bragg, jcl}@microsoft.com
arxiv-2307-15039.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Akanksha Saran, Jacob Alber, Cyril Zhang, Ann Paradiso, Danielle Bragg, John Langford, Microsoft Research NYC, Microsoft Research New England, Microsoft Research Redmond {akanksha.saran, jacob.alber, cyrilzhangannpar, danielle.bragg, jcl}@microsoft.com. Gaze tracking devices have the potential to greatly expand interactivity, yet miscalibration remains a significant barrier to use. As devices miscalibrate, people tend to compensate by intentionally offsetting their gaze, which makes detecting miscalibration from eye signals difficult.

arxiv-2401-07437.title: BoNuS: Boundary Mining for Nuclei Segmentation with Partial Point Labels Thanks: Y. Lin, Z. Wang, D. Zhang, and K.-T. Cheng are with the Department of Computer Science and Engineering, The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology, Hong Kong, China. E-mail: {yi.lin, zwangek}@connect.ust.hk; {do
arxiv-2401-07437.creator: Yi Lin, Zeyu Wang, Dong Zhang
arxiv-2401-07437.description: Abstract Nuclei segmentation is a fundamental prerequisite in the digital pathology workflow. The development of automated methods for nuclei segmentation enables quantitative analysis of the wide existence and large variances in nuclei morphometry in histopathology images. However, manual annotation of tens of thousands of nuclei is tedious and time-consuming, which requires significant amount of human effort and domain-specific expertise.

arxiv-2402-09094.title: Unity is Strength: Enhancing Precision in Reentrancy Vulnerability Detection of Smart Contract Analysis Tools
arxiv-2402-09094.creator: Zexu Wang, Jiachi Chen, Zibin Zheng, Peilin Zheng, Yu Zhang, Weizhe Zhang
arxiv-2402-09094.description: Abstract Reentrancy is one of the most notorious vulnerabilities in smart contracts, resulting in significant digital asset losses. However, many previous works indicate that current Reentrancy detection tools suffer from high false positive rates. Even worse, recent years have witnessed the emergence of new Reentrancy attack patterns fueled by intricate and diverse vulnerability exploit mechanisms.

arxiv-2404-17730.title: Bridging the Social & Technical Divide in Augmentative and Alternative Communication (AAC) Applications for Autistic Adults CCS: Human-centered computing Accessibility technologies CCS: Human-centered computing Accessibility systems and tools CCS: Human-centered computing Accessibility design and ev
arxiv-2404-17730.creator: Lara J. Martin, Malathy Nagalakshmi
arxiv-2404-17730.description: Abstract . Natural Language Processing (NLP) techniques are being used more frequently to improve high-tech Augmentative and Alternative Communication (AAC), but many of these techniques are integrated without the inclusion of the users’ perspectives. As many of these tools are created with children in mind, autistic adults are often neglected in the design of AAC tools to begin with.

arxiv-2408-13565.title: CONVEX POLYGONS
arxiv-2408-13565.creator: AND THE ISOPERIMETRIC PROBLEM
arxiv-2408-13565.description: Abstract Anisa M. H. Chorwadwala and A. R. Aithal ABSTRACT. In this article, we prove that there exists a unique perimeter minimizer among all piecewise smooth simple closed curves in M^{2}_{\kappa} enclosing area A>0 ( A\leq 2\pi if \kappa=1 ), and it is a circle in M^{2}_{\kappa} of radius AS_{\kappa}\left(\sqrt{A\,(4\pi-\kappa\,A)}/(2\pi)\right) , where AS_{\kappa}(t):=\begin{cases}t&\text{if $\kappa=0$},\\ \arcsin(t)&\text{if $\kappa=1$},\\ \sinh^{-1}(t)&\text{if $\kappa=-1$}.

arxiv-2409-05538.title: Probing Optoelectronic Properties of Stable Vacancy-Ordered Double Perovskites: Insights from Many-Body Perturbation Theory
arxiv-2409-05538.creator: Surajit Adhikari*, Priya Johari
arxiv-2409-05538.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Surajit Adhikari*, Priya Johari. A 2 BX 6 vacancy-ordered double perovskites (VODPs) have captured substantial research interest in the scientific community as they offer environmentally friendly and stable alternatives to lead halide perovskites. In this study, we investigate Rb 2 BCl 6 (B = Ti, Se, Ru, Pd) VODPs as promising optoelectronic materials employing state-of-the-art first-principles-based methodologies, specifically density functional theory combined with density functional perturbation theory (DFPT) and many-body perturbation theory [within the framework of GW and BSE].

arxiv-2409-11113.title: CageCoOpt: Enhancing Manipulation Robustness through Caging-Guided Morphology and Policy Co-Optimization
arxiv-2409-11113.creator: Yifei Dong, Shaohang Han, Xianyi Cheng, Werner Friedl, Rafael I. Cabral Muchacho, Máximo A. Roa, Jana Tumova, Florian T. Pokorny
arxiv-2409-11113.description: Abstract Uncertainties in contact dynamics and object geometry remain significant barriers to robust robotic manipulation. Caging mitigates these uncertainties by constraining an object’s mobility without requiring precise contact modeling. However, existing caging research has largely treated morphology and policy optimization as separate problems, overlooking their inherent synergy.

arxiv-2411-17251.title: Interpretable Dynamic Graph Neural Networks for Small Occluded Object Detection and Tracking
arxiv-2411-17251.creator: Shahriar Soudeep, Md Abrar Jahin, and M. F. Mridha
arxiv-2411-17251.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Shahriar Soudeep, Md Abrar Jahin, and M. F. Mridha. The detection and tracking of small, occluded objects—such as pedestrians, cyclists, and motorbikes—pose significant challenges for traffic surveillance systems because of their erratic movement, frequent occlusion, and poor visibility in dynamic urban environments. Traditional methods like YOLO11, while proficient in spatial feature extraction for precise detection, often struggle with these small and dynamically moving objects, particularly in handling real-time data updates and resource efficiency.

arxiv-2503-16829.title: Quantitative stratification for the fractional Allen-Cahn equation and stationary nonlocal minimal surface Thanks: K. Wang is supported by National Key R&D Program of China (No. 2022YFA1005602) and the National Natural Science Foundation of China (No. 12131017 and No. 12221001). J. Wei is partially
arxiv-2503-16829.creator: Kelei Wang †, Juncheng Wei ∗, Ke Wu ∗
arxiv-2503-16829.description: Abstract . We study properties of solutions to the fractional Allen-Cahn equation when s ∈ ( 0 , 1 / 2 ) s\in(0,1/2) and dimension n ≥ 2 n\geq 2 . By applying the quantitative stratification principle developed by Naber and Valtorta, we obtain an optimal quantitative estimate on the transition set.

arxiv-2509-01360.title: M 3 Ret: Unleashing Zero-shot Multimodal Medical Image Retrieval via Self-Supervision
arxiv-2509-01360.creator: Che Liu, Zheng Jiang, Chengyu Fang, Heng Guo, Yan-Jie Zhou, Jiaqi Qu, Le Lu, Minfeng Xu
arxiv-2509-01360.description: Abstract Medical image retrieval is essential for clinical decision-making and translational research, relying on discriminative visual representations. Yet, current methods remain fragmented, relying on separate architectures and training strategies for 2D, 3D, and video-based medical data. This modality-specific design hampers scalability and inhibits the development of unified representations.

arxiv-2511-08218.title: Who benefits from increases in military spending? An empirical analysis. Corresponding author: Haroon Mumtaz ( h.mumtaz@qmul.ac.uk ). Do not circulate without authors’ permission. The views expressed in this paper are solely the responsibility of the authors and should not be interpreted as reflecti
arxiv-2511-08218.creator: John Beirne, Haroon Mumtaz, Donghyun Park, Gazi Salah Uddin, Angeliki Theophilopoulou
arxiv-2511-08218.description: Abstract This paper investigates the heterogeneous effects of military spending news shocks on household income and wealth inequality for a large, panel of advanced and emerging economies. Confirming prior literature, we find that military spending news shocks lead to persistent increases in aggregate output and Total Factor Productivity. Our primary contribution is documenting contrasting distributional impacts.

arxiv-2603-13744.creator: Shiyun Zhang, Yibo Yao, Haoquan Long, Dingwen Tao, Guangming Tan, Wei-Hua Wang, Yuan-Chao Hu

britannica-1911-choiseul-cesar.title: Choiseul, César (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)
britannica-1911-choiseul-cesar.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-choiseul-cesar.description: Article 'Choiseul, César' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 6), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. and diplomatist, generally known for the best part of his life as the marshal du Plessis-Praslin, came of the old French family of Choiseul, which arose in the valley of the Upper Marne in the 10th century and divided into many branches, three of the names of which, Hostel, Praslin and du Plessis, were borne, at one time or another, by the subject of this article.

gao-gaoreports-gao-08-738t.creator: U.S. Government Accountability Office
gao-gaoreports-gao-08-738t.description: Information Management: Challenges in Implementing an Electronic Records Archive (2008).

pmc-10574802.title: Anatomical and Transcriptome Analyses of Moso Bamboo Culm Neck Growth: Unveiling Key Insights
pmc-10574802.creator: Lin Guo, Tianguo Chen, Xue Chu, Kai Sun, Fen Yu, Feng Que, Zishan Ahmad, Qiang Wei, Muthusamy Ramakrishnan, Nobutoshi Yamaguchi
pmc-10574802.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). The Moso bamboo culm neck, connected with the rhizome and the shoot bud, is an important hub for connecting and transporting the aboveground and belowground systems of bamboo for the shoot bud development and rapid growth. Our previous study revealed that the culm neck generally undergoes six different developmental stages (CNS1–CNS6), according to the primary thickening growth of the underground shoot bud. However, the molecular mechanism of the culm neck development remains unknown.

pmc-10655486.title: Skills in handling Turbuhaler, Diskus in the west of China
pmc-10655486.creator: Wei Wei, Dong Wang, Weiting Liu, Hui Du, Zhiye Zhang, Shengying Che, Rui Ding, YanBiao Yang
pmc-10655486.description: ObjectiveThe purpose of this study was to evaluate the inhaler skills of patients with asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease in a hospital in western China after receiving one medication education by pharmacists and the factors related to these skills.MethodsWe included 96 subjects using Turbuhaler and 74 subjects using Diskus in a hospital in western China.

pmc-10740674.title: Hypomagnetic Conditions and Their Biological Action (Review)
pmc-10740674.creator: Ruslan M Sarimov, Dmitriy A Serov, Sergey V Gudkov, Daniel R Kattnig, Clarice D Aiello
pmc-10740674.description: Simple SummaryThe Earth’s magnetic field is vital for life to exist. If the field becomes weaker, it’s known as hypomagnetic conditions. Studying the impact of hypomagnetic conditions on living beings is significant for multiple reasons. Firstly, it helps us comprehend the biological consequences and learn more about how the magnetic field interacts with living organisms.

pmc-11479542.title: Transcriptome analysis reveals key regulatory networks and genes involved in the acquisition of cold stress memory in pepper seedlings
pmc-11479542.creator: Jian Li, Ping Yang, Hongbo Fu, Juan Li, Yanzhuang Wang, Keyan Zhu, Jihua Yu, Jie Li
pmc-11479542.description: Temperature is an important limiting factor in the counter-seasonal cultivation of pepper. Currently, there are no studies on transcriptomic analysis of ‘cold stress memory’ in pepper. In this study, in order to understand the mechanism of ‘cold stress memory’ in pepper (Capsicum annuum L.

pmc-11548127.title: Sensing the Changes in Stratum Corneum Using Fourier Transform Infrared Microspectroscopy and Hyperspectral Data Processing
pmc-11548127.creator: Krzysztof Banas, Agnieszka M Banas, Giorgia Pastorin, Ngai Mun Hong, Shikhar Gupta, Katarzyna Dziedzic-Kocurek, Mark B H Breese, A G Unil Perera
pmc-11548127.description: The stratum corneum (SC) forms the outermost layer of the skin, playing a critical role in preventing water loss and protecting against external biological and chemical threats. Approximately 90% of the SC consists of large, flat corneocytes, yet its barrier function primarily relies on the intercellular lipid matrix that surrounds these cells.

pmc-12426246.title: Development and validation of clinical prediction models for cardiorespiratory fitness in atrial fibrillation patients following radiofrequency catheter ablation
pmc-12426246.creator: Guiling Zhao, Jian Sun, Qianji Che, Wenqing Xu, Mengmeng Song, Doa El-Ansary, Roger Adams, Jia Han, Shu Meng, Yigang Li
pmc-12426246.description: BackgroundAssessment of cardiorespiratory fitness (CRF) is imperative in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) who have had radiofrequency catheter ablation (RFCA). This study aimed to develop and validate CRF prediction models in this population.Methods141 AF patients with RFCA were recruited. The cardiopulmonary exercise test was used to assess CRF with VO2peak and METsmax.

pmc-12429320.title: Rodent Models of Lung Disease: A Road Map for Translational Research
pmc-12429320.creator: Jerome Cantor, Roberto Plebani
pmc-12429320.description: Animal models provide a controlled and reproducible environment for investigating the pathogenesis of human lung diseases. In many cases, the morphological changes associated with a particular model may resemble those seen in their human counterparts, but the corresponding biochemical events may differ, and their timeframe may be significantly reduced.

pmc-12436373.title: The role of Caveolin-1 in tumor-derived extracellular vesicle biology and its implications
pmc-12436373.creator: Satish Kailasam Mani, Christophe Lamaze, Cristian Saquel
pmc-12436373.description: Tumor-derived extracellular vesicles (TEVs) are increasingly recognized as key mediators of intercellular communication between cancer cells and their environment, a process crucial for tumor progression. TEVs can act locally on neighboring cells or travel long distances to impact remote tissues, thereby promoting tumor growth, cell invasion, pre-metastatic niche formation, and ultimately, metastasis.

pmc-12659347.title: Fundamental sex differences in cocaine-induced plasticity of D1R- and D2R-MSNs in the mouse nucleus accumbens core
pmc-12659347.creator: Andrew D Chapp, Hannah M McMullan, Chau-Mi H Phan, Pramit P Jagtap, Mark J Thomas, Paul G Mermelstein
pmc-12659347.description: BackgroundCocaine-induced changes in nucleus accumbens shell (NAcSh) medium spiny neurons (MSNs) differ based on dopamine receptor subtype expression, the sex of the animal, and for females, phase of the estrous cycle. These findings highlight the need to account for both sex and estrous cycle when studying drug-mediated alterations in neurophysiology.

pmc-13084324.title: Long‐term intermittent catheterization: Safety and outcomes from a prospective observational study
pmc-13084324.creator: Peter Taffo, Gerard Amarenco, Carina Andersson, Nicola Morris, Jan Hörling
pmc-13084324.description: ObjectivesThe aim of this study was to evaluate long‐term safety, urological complication rates and quality of life (QoL) associated with urethral intermittent catheterization (IC) over a 5‐year follow‐up in adult, established, experienced subjects with longstanding IC use.Patients and MethodsProspective, noninterventional, observational cohort study at three European sites.

pmc-13220953.title: One-year impact of an ambulatory pulmonary curriculum for fellows leveraging adult learning theory
pmc-13220953.creator: Kathleen A McAvoy, Katherine A Gielissen, Shyoko Honiden, Jennifer D Possick
pmc-13220953.description: BackgroundIn pulmonary and critical care medicine (PCCM) fellowship, inpatient training is often prioritized over outpatient learning, resulting in fellows’ dissatisfaction with their ambulatory education. Additional challenges limit the use of best practices for teaching and learning in graduate medical education.

pmc-13223196.title: Sensitivity of current Tropilaelaps mercedesae monitoring methods in Apis mellifera colonies
pmc-13223196.creator: Rogan Tokach, Dan Aurell, Bajaree Chuttong, Geoffrey R Williams
pmc-13223196.description: The parasitic mite Tropilaelaps mercedesae (Anderson & Morgan) has recently been confirmed in western honey bee (Apis mellifera L.) colonies in western Asia and eastern Europe, marking a range expansion that necessitates effective monitoring methods to rapidly detect introductions into new regions, as well as promote integrated pest management where it is established.

pmc-13295669.title: Predicting Recurrence Risk of Glioblastoma Based on Preoperative-Postoperative Longitudinal MRI: A Multicenter Study
pmc-13295669.creator: Chengwei Chen, Fan Guo, Dong Huang, Yao Zheng, Yuefei Feng, Tianci Liu, Yuxuan Yao, Jie Wei, Minwen Zheng, Yang Liu
pmc-13295669.description: Glioblastoma has a high recurrence rate, yet conventional single-time-point imaging fails to capture the dynamic tumor evolution before and after surgery. This study aims to develop a deep learning model based on preoperative and postoperative longitudinal MRI to predict postoperative recurrence risk by capturing imaging dynamics.

pmc-13554641.title: Development and interpretability of a machine learning model for postoperative hypothermia prediction in placenta previa Cesarean section: A retrospective cohort study
pmc-13554641.creator: Yu Zhu, Daoqing Xie, Renrui Liang, Cheng-Mao Zhou
pmc-13554641.description: ObjectiveTo develop and validate an explainable machine learning prediction model for perioperative hypothermia in patients undergoing cesarean delivery for placenta previa, and to identify key predictive factors to support clinical individualized temperature management and nursing decision-making.MethodsThis study is a retrospective secondary analysis conducted using BioStudies public databases.

pmc-13612246.title: Diabetes exacerbates experimental peri-implantitis in mice with elevated IL-17A-associated inflammation and IL-17F upregulation
pmc-13612246.creator: Takumi Memida, Jacques Christopher Jaar, Tsute Chen, Guoqin Cao, Nanako Kuriki, Elaheh Dalir Abdolahinia, Satoru Shindo, Shohei Yamashita, Sunniva Ruiz, Avissasadat Meraji, Alex Albu, Motoki Okamoto, Xuesong He, Saynur Vardar, Maiko Suzuki, Jiang Lin, Toshihisa Kawai, Xiaozhe Han
pmc-13612246.description: This study investigated the role of interleukin-17 (IL-17) and the oral microbiome in peri-implant inflammation and bone loss under hyperglycemic and normoglycemic conditions. Wild-type (WT) and diabetic (db/db) mice with maxillary implants underwent ligature placement with or without IL-17A neutralization. Bone loss, osteoclast activity, inflammatory cytokines, Th17/Treg balance, and expression of IL-17Family members were analyzed.

pmc-13680869.title: Advanced Cardiovascular‐Kidney‐Metabolic Risk and Risk‐Factor Control in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes Without Established Cardiovascular Disease
pmc-13680869.creator: Hai Nguyen Ngoc Dang, The Trung Le, Anh Kiem Pham, Linh Duy Le, Nam Van Duc Nguyen, Thanh Thien Tran, Thinh Ba Le, Ny Ha Tuyet Le, Nam Van Le, Hau Phuc Tran, Hung Minh Vu, Duong Hung Tran, Bich Ngoc Hoang Thi, Huy Nhu Pham, Hieu Minh Le, Thang Chi Doan, Binh Anh Ho, Tien Anh Hoang, Minh Van Huynh, T
pmc-13680869.description: BackgroundCardiovascular‐kidney‐metabolic (CKM) risk stratification may identify patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) who require more intensive primary prevention, but real‐world data from Vietnam are limited. We aimed to describe advanced CKM risk and risk‐factor control in Vietnamese patients with T2DM without established cardiovascular disease (CVD).MethodsThis multicenter cross‐sectional study enrolled 1436 adults with T2DM without CVD in Vietnam.
